summary: This bill repeals section 213 of the Continuing Appropriations Act, 2026, eliminating requirements to notify Senate offices about legal process for disclosing Senate data.

scores.thoughts: The bill repeals a narrow procedural requirement related to Senate data notifications. It has no provisions affecting government budgets, appropriations levels, or spending priorities.
The bill contains no tax-related provisions, rates, credits, or enforcement mechanisms.
No content in the bill addresses healthcare policy, coverage, or markets.
The legislation does not mention firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No references to immigration, borders, visas, or related enforcement.
The bill is silent on reproductive rights or abortion access.
No impact on defense spending, military policy, or national security appropriations.
No environmental regulations, climate provisions, or energy policy changes.
The bill does not address welfare programs, entitlements, or social services.
No provisions related to schools, funding, or education policy.
The legislation contains nothing about drug enforcement, decriminalization, or substance regulation.
No changes to sentencing, policing, or criminal procedure beyond a narrow Senate data notification repeal.
No trade agreements, tariffs, or globalization measures.
The bill has no fiscal impact on deficits or debt reduction strategies.
No provisions addressing LGBTQ protections or related civil rights.
The bill does not mention foreign assistance or international aid.
No election administration, voting access, or campaign finance content.

While the bill repeals a notification rule concerning disclosure of Senate data, the change is narrowly procedural and internal to Congress with no broader implications for technology regulation or privacy policy.
No labor, union, or workplace policy provisions.
The bill does not engage with religious exemptions or anti-discrimination rules.
